payload.title: [blob-gc-2] GC silently never runs for non-default apps in a multi-app server (orphan leak; undocumented)
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING blob-gc-2 (medium/correctness, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/blobs/gc-job.ts
LINES: 117-146, 155-211

WHAT: FrickJobContext (apps/server/src/jobs/registry.ts:17-25) carries tenantId but NO appId, and runOrphanedBlobGc never threads an appId. collectDeclaredReferencedBlobIds calls store.objects.list(tenantId, objectName) (line 135) and the GC calls store.blobs.listAllOldestFirst(tenantId) (line 170), deleteContent/deleteMetadata (gc-job.ts:250-255) — every one of these defaults appId to DEFAULT_APP_ID (see object-store.ts:188-200 and blob-store.ts:169-196). The recurring scheduler also enqueues the blob.gc job via store.jobs.enqueue({tenantId, jobType,...}) with no appId (recurring.ts:133-139), so it lands in the default app's partition. Net effect: in a multi-app server (FR-153), the GC only ever scans and reclaims `_default`-app blobs/objects; blobs owned by every non-default app are never examined and never reclaimed. This is consistent (it can't cross-delete, since blob_metadata PK is blob_id-global and the create guard prevents cross-app ownership), so it is a storage LEAK, not data loss — but it is undocumented: the module header and CHANGELOG (line 35) describe GC as operating 'per tenant' with no mention that it is also limited to the default app. The isReferenced hook is likewise given only {tenantId, blobId} (gc-job.ts:67-70), so it cannot disambiguate apps even if GC were extended.

IMPACT: Operators of multi-app deployments believe orphaned-blob GC is reclaiming storage for all apps when it only touches the default app — unbounded storage growth for non-default apps with no error or log. The isReferenced contract is also app-blind.

SUGGESTED FIX: Thread appId through the GC: add appId to FrickJobContext / job rows, fan the recurring sweep out per (tenant, app), pass appId into listAllOldestFirst/objects.list/deleteContent/deleteMetadata, and add appId to BlobIsReferencedHook args. At minimum, document the default-app-only limitation prominently in the module header, ServerOptions.blobGc doc, and CHANGELOG.
